chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl, from Safwan, and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Cast [the pebbles] each day at the time of the sun's decline, and say as you said when you cast the Jamarat al-Aqaba. Begin with the first Jamarah, cast it from its left side, from the bottom of the stream, and say as you said on the Day of Sacrifice. Then stand to the left of the path, face the Qiblah, praise Allah, extol Him, and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). Then advance slightly, supplicate, and ask Him to accept [your worship] from you. Then advance again and do the same for the second, and act as you did with the first. Stand and supplicate to Allah as you supplicated. Then proceed to the third, and upon you is calmness and dignity, and do not stand at it.

key_terms.بَطْنِ الْمَسِيلِ: The bottom of the stream/wadi (location for casting)
key_terms.جَمْرَةَ الْعَقَبَةِ: The first and largest Jamarah pillar in Mina
key_terms.يَوْمِ النَّحْرِ: The Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications and actions when casting the Jamarat during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* provides a detailed procedural guide for the Rami al-Jamarat ritual, emphasizing the imitation of the Prophet’s actions at the first Jamarah and the specific etiquette of standing and supplicating at the second. It highlights the Shia emphasis on *sakinah* (tranquility) and *waqar* (dignity) during the ritual, distinguishing the third Jamarah where one proceeds without stopping, thereby linking physical action with spiritual mindfulness.
